Ziang Shoe's shop, 348 Chekiang Road (Louza).

st organs" purporting to have been issued by the Commu-
nist Centre, instructing all communist members through-
out the country to read all communist papers, particu-
larly the Sing Hwa Daily (published in Hankow), in order
to refresh their knowledge of the communistic doctrine.
2. Lecture given in Hankow by Tseu Ung-lai 周恩来, a

and bigger victories" dealing with battles recently
fought in South Shantung.

cal Council" analysing the organization and power of
the above council, which was recently formed in Hankow.
4. Article entitled "The present Chinese Youth Movement
and its Object" advising all Chinese able-bodied
youths to join the nation-wide anti-invasion campaign
in order to expel all Japanese militarists from China
and lead the Chinese people toward emancipation.

ASSISTANCE TO SPECIAL BRANCH

Interrogated at this Station by D.S.I. Logan, D.S. McKeown and Inspector Shih Sze Chien attached to the Special Branch, the arrested person (1st accused) admitted that part of the seized literature was handed to him for sale by the proprietor of the Dah Tsoong (大中) Book Factory at 329/568 Sinza Road named Tsou Yoong (周容) and that the remainder by another news-vendor named Ling Lih (林立) prior to his arrest.

Tsai Liu and C.D.C. 150 accompanied by detectives attached to the Special Branch visited the 1st mentioned address at 329/568 Sinza Road, where the proprietor of the above Book Factory Tsou Yoong, 26, Chekiang, was also taken into custody. A search was made in the front upper room of the above address, where a large quantity of periodicals and newspapers of similar nature were seized.

The 6th accused Tsang Hung Dao who is at present
detained in the French Police Headquarters was questioned
by Special Branch detectives during the morning of August 11
regarding the source of origin of the books entitled
"Collection of Editorials of the Sing Hwa Jih Pao." 新華日報評論集
According to Tsang's statement, sometime ago, one Yue
Tsoong (余忠) approached him in the Hwa Mei Publishing
Company, 172 Avenue Edward VII, where the 6th accused was
employed, and requested the company to act as sales agent
for the books above mentioned in return for a commission
from the sale of same. The matter was referred by the
6th accused to Mr. Tsu Tsao Dong (朱草同), the Chinese manager of
the company, who was stated to have accepted the offer.
Tsu, however, later discovered the books to contain
articles of a very strong anti-Japanese nature and
cancelled the agreement. An announcement to the effect
was published through the press on June 25, 1938, which
reads as follows :-

"Notice of the Hwa Mei Publishing Company

We are surprised to learn that copies of a book
entitled "A Collection of Editorials published by the
Hsin Hwa Jih Pao" in which appears the information:
"General Sales Agent: The Hwa Mei Publishing Co.,
172 Avenue Edward VII, Telephone No.13013," have
been in circulation in this locality recently.
We have never undertaken the sale of periodicals on
behalf of others nor have we made any arrangements

sale of these publications I reaped good profits. Following
the withdrawal of Chinese armies from Shanghai area, the local
police authorities tightened its control over the sale of all
books and periodicals of an anti-Japanese nature, in consequence
of which I had to wind up my business. Between November, 1937
and March, 1938, I was unemployed. In March, 1938 I obtained
employment in the News Digest Press through the introduction of
one Mr. Doo (杜) of the above Press, who was an old customer

周 莹    汪 英
The 1st accused Wong Ying and the 3rd accused
Tseu Yoong were removed from Chengtu Road Station to
Headquarters on August 15 and carefully questioned
between 9.30 a.m. and 4.15 p.m. by Special Branch
detectives. According to the statement of the 3rd
accused, from whose home some 3,000 copies of anti-
Japanese and communistic booklets and periodicals were
seized, the publications in question were mostly bought
from various book stores in Canton and Hongkong, He in
turn sold them to various local news vendors mainly
through the 1st accused. The periodicals "Emancipation"
and "Unity", he asserted, were obtained from one Siao Sz 小四子
Ts, who he believes is an agent of a local national
salvation organization and are believed to have been
printed locally. He, however, did not know details
regarding the organization nor did he know the address of
Siao Sz Ts. The 3rd accused stated that he engaged in
the above described business purely for monetary gain and
he ran the risk of being arrested simply because the
profit from the sale of such books was so much greater
than could be obtained from the sale of other ordinary
books and periodicals. The mimeograph set found in the
home of the 3rd accused was, according to the 3rd accused,
used for printing the catalogue and price lists of all
new books. An examination of the set resulted in the
discovery of an old stencil paper thereon, and the
statement of 3rd accused in this respect was verified.

Date August 30, 1938

Subject Chinese arrested in possession of anti-Japanese and
Communist Literature - released

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie

The 3rd accused Tseu Yoong (周容), the 4th
accused Wu Liang (吴良) and the 5th accused Wu Ching
Tsung (吴镜椿) were released on August 26th and the
2nd accused Ling Lih (林立) was released on August
29th on the instructions of D.C. (Special Branch).
Before release each of the accused signed a bond and
furnished a guarantor, promising to refrain from engaging
in political activities or the sale of political
publications in future.

With reference to the 6th accused Tsang Hung Dao
(张洪涛) who was arrested in the French Concession
on August 10th, the French Police were communicated with
on August 26th regarding his release and Special Branch
were informed to make arrangements for the furnishing of
guarantees. However on proceeding to the home of the
6th accused at Lane 685, No.41 Rue Amiral Bayle,
detectives ascertained that the man had been released
by the French Police on August 17th, no intimation of
this having been received by Special Branch.

With regard to the 1st accused Wong Ying (汪英),
he is unable to supply a guarantor for his future conduct
and is still detained in Chengtu Road Station.

Instructions are solicited as to the action to
be taken with regard to this accused.

R. W. Mac Adie
